analysis.title: What Matters Today: Jensen is back. NVDA Soars, Memory - Strong 2027, A More Measured 2028, The Causes and Consequences of a Low-Hire, Low-Fire Labor Market
key_insights: NVDA added about $940bn of market cap in one day on GIR's take on Jensen's reinstatement. The US desk saw an early chase with the stock up more than 30% and macro hedges being taken off.

HFs were busier than long-only accounts, covering short books in NVDA, select tech names and macro expressions. NDX constituent volumes were up about 60%, and the desk's activity level was a 5 on a 1-10 scale.
After two weeks of heavy long-only supply in NVDA, supply abatement was seen as a large part of the move's magnitude.
NDX rose more than 5% in a single day. Comparable moves (Apr'25, Nov'22, Mar'20, Dec'18) each came at or near local market lows.

Investor feedback is mixed with more questions than strong opinions. Bulls cite 'nobody left to sell' positioning and a sentiment-driven AI/Semis bear market. Bears cite China, shell/permitting, ROIs and token trajectory, and see limited upside above pre-Election levels.

GS expects meaningful memory undersupply in 2027, especially DRAM and HBM, but a smaller undersupply in 2028E. Conventional DRAM price forecast is now +32%/-19% YoY for 2027E/2028E (from +32%/-5%), and NAND is +20%/-21% (from +30%/-14%).
GS raised HBM TAM estimates to US$60bn/US$200bn/US$237bn for 2026E/2027E/2028E.
Samsung and Hynix share prices are seen as pricing zero AI capex growth in 2028E and an additional 40% ASP decline vs GS's base case. GS stays constructive given about 20% shareholder return yields.
LTA default risk looks limited, since conventional DRAM prices would need to fall more than 32-54% below GS's base case over two years before customers have an incentive to default.

For Kioxia, GS lowers FY3/28-29 OP estimates by 15%/30% (FY3/27E unchanged) on price declines from Apr-Jun 2027. EPS cuts are modest because of larger implied buybacks, with 100% surplus FCF return policy implying over 30% FY3/28E TSR yield.
GS models CXMT generating HBM revenue from next year, limited to HBM2E and HBM3 and a small fraction of TAM.
Low US labor turnover is driven mostly by lower churn (job-to-job moves) rather than job reallocation. Aging workforce, better matching and an emerging AI effect are cited drivers.
Depressed churn weighs on YoY wage growth by about 0.3pp. GS expects turnover to pick up somewhat but warns persistent low turnover could dampen productivity growth.

market_movers.rationale: Stock soared on Jensen's reinstatement, adding about $940bn of market cap in one day, helped by supply abatement and short covering.
Samsung (SEC): GS stays constructive. Shares price in zero AI capex growth in 2028E and about 20% shareholder return yield.
SK Hynix: GS stays constructive despite a more measured 2028E, as downside risks look priced in.
Kioxia: FY3/28-29 OP estimates cut 15%/30%, EPS revisions modest given buyback capacity and 100% surplus FCF return policy.

sector_views.rationale: Strong 2027 undersupply in DRAM and HBM, with 2028 more measured but downside risks seen as priced in.

earnings_insights: Kioxia: GS cuts FY3/28 and FY3/29 operating profit estimates by 15% and 30% (FY3/27E unchanged). Management policy of returning 100% of surplus FCF could mean over 30% FY3/28E TSR yield.

macro_indicators.indicator: Wage growth drag from depressed churn
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS estimate that low job-switching holds wage growth below what the unemployment rate implies.
GS 2028 forecast cut from -5%, signalling a softer memory pricing cycle.

Rally may stall near pre-Election levels and below the 200-dma.
2028 memory oversupply risk and LTA default risk.
Persistently low labor turnover could dampen productivity.
